title: Every AWS Service on the Free Plan

categories.name: Compute
categories.blurb: Run code, from full virtual servers to functions that only exist while a request is running.

services.name: Amazon EC2
services.desc: Virtual servers in the cloud. Pick the CPU, memory, operating system and storage, then start and stop machines on demand.

services.name: AWS Lambda
services.desc: Runs your code in response to events, like an HTTP request or a file upload, without any servers to manage. You pay per request and per millisecond.

services.name: Amazon Lightsail
services.desc: The simplest way to launch a server, website or database, with bundled storage and networking at a fixed monthly price.

services.name: AWS Elastic Beanstalk
services.desc: Upload your web app and it handles the servers, load balancing, scaling and health monitoring for you.

services.name: AWS Batch
services.desc: Queues and runs large numbers of batch jobs, picking the right amount of compute and scaling it up and down.

services.name: EC2 Image Builder
services.desc: Automates building, testing and patching the machine images and container images your servers start from.

services.name: Application Auto Scaling
services.desc: Adds or removes capacity for services like ECS, DynamoDB and Aurora automatically as demand changes.

services.name: Elastic Load Balancing
services.desc: Spreads incoming traffic across servers, containers or functions, and stops sending it to anything unhealthy.

services.name: AWS Serverless Application Repository
services.desc: A catalog of ready-made serverless apps you can deploy to your account in a few clicks.

services.name: AWS Launch Wizard
services.desc: Guided setup for complex software such as Microsoft SQL Server and SAP, sizing and deploying the AWS resources for you.

categories.name: Containers
categories.blurb: Package apps into containers and run them on managed clusters.

services.name: Amazon Elastic Container Service (ECS)
services.desc: AWS's own container orchestrator. Run Docker containers on EC2 or on serverless Fargate capacity.

services.name: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS)
services.desc: Managed Kubernetes. AWS runs the control plane so you only manage your workloads.

services.name: Amazon EKS Anywhere
services.desc: Run the same EKS-style Kubernetes on your own hardware, in your data center or on VMware.

services.name: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR)
services.desc: Private registry for storing, scanning and sharing your container images.

services.name: Amazon ECR Public
services.desc: Public registry for publishing container images that anyone can pull.

services.name: AWS App2Container
services.desc: Command-line tool that packages existing Java and .NET apps into containers, ready for ECS or EKS.

categories.name: Storage and Backup
categories.blurb: Keep files, disks and backups safe and available.

services.name: Amazon S3
services.desc: Object storage for any amount of data: files, images, backups, static websites and data lakes.

services.name: Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS)
services.desc: Hard drives for EC2 servers. Block storage volumes with snapshots you can copy and restore.

services.name: Amazon Elastic File System (EFS)
services.desc: A shared file system that many servers and containers can mount at once, and that grows and shrinks automatically.

services.name: AWS Backup
services.desc: One place to schedule, manage and audit backups across EC2, EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, EFS, S3 and more.

services.name: AWS DataSync
services.desc: Moves large amounts of data between on-premises storage, other clouds and AWS storage, fast and on a schedule.

services.name: AWS Backint Agent
services.desc: SAP-certified agent that backs up SAP HANA databases on EC2 straight to Amazon S3.

categories.name: Databases
categories.blurb: Managed relational, NoSQL, in-memory and time-series databases.

services.name: Amazon RDS
services.desc: Managed relational databases: MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, SQL Server and Oracle. AWS handles patching, backups and failover.

services.name: Amazon Aurora
services.desc: AWS's high-performance MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible database, with a serverless option that scales automatically.

services.name: Amazon Aurora DSQL
services.desc: Serverless, distributed PostgreSQL-compatible database built for always-on apps, with no servers to size.

services.name: Amazon DynamoDB
services.desc: Serverless NoSQL key-value and document database with single-digit-millisecond responses at any scale.

services.name: Amazon ElastiCache
services.desc: Managed in-memory caching with Valkey, Redis OSS or Memcached, to make apps and databases faster.

services.name: Amazon Timestream
services.desc: Time-series database for metrics, IoT readings and other data that arrives as a stream of timestamped values.

services.name: AWS SQL Workbench
services.desc: Browser-based SQL editor with notebooks, charts and AI-assisted query writing, for exploring data in AWS databases such as Amazon Redshift.

categories.name: Analytics and Data
categories.blurb: Query, move, clean, govern and visualize data.

services.name: Amazon Athena
services.desc: Run SQL directly on files stored in S3. No servers or loading step, and you pay per query.

services.name: AWS Glue
services.desc: Serverless data integration: discover, catalog, clean and transform data with ETL jobs.

services.name: AWS Lake Formation
services.desc: Builds and secures a data lake on S3, with fine-grained permissions down to rows and columns.

services.name: Amazon DataZone
services.desc: A data catalog and portal for finding, sharing and governing data across teams.

services.name: Amazon OpenSearch Service
services.desc: Managed OpenSearch for full-text search, log analytics and vector search.

services.name: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless
services.desc: OpenSearch without clusters to manage. Capacity scales automatically with your search and analytics workload.

services.name: Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow
services.desc: Managed Apache Airflow for scheduling and running data pipelines.

services.name: AWS Data Pipeline
services.desc: An older service for moving and processing data between AWS compute and storage on a schedule.

services.name: AWS Entity Resolution
services.desc: Matches and links records about the same customer, product or business across different datasets.

services.name: Amazon AppFlow
services.desc: No-code data transfers between SaaS apps such as Salesforce, Slack and Zendesk and AWS services like S3.

services.name: Amazon Quick
services.desc: AI-powered workspace that combines business intelligence dashboards (Quick Sight), research and chat agents over your company's data.
services.note: Only the Quick Free and Quick Plus editions are available.

categories.name: AI and Machine Learning
categories.blurb: Foundation models, agents, and ready-made AI for images, speech and language.

services.name: Amazon Bedrock
services.desc: API access to foundation models from Anthropic, Amazon, Meta, Mistral and others, plus tools for knowledge bases, guardrails and agents.

services.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
services.desc: Infrastructure to deploy and run AI agents securely at scale: runtime, memory, identity, tool gateway and observability, with any framework or model.

services.name: Amazon SageMaker
services.desc: AWS's unified platform for data, analytics and AI, bringing data processing, SQL analytics and model development together.

services.name: Amazon SageMaker AI
services.desc: Build, train, tune and deploy machine learning models with managed notebooks, training jobs and hosted endpoints.

services.name: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio
services.desc: One development environment for working with data, analytics and AI models across SageMaker and Bedrock.

services.name: Amazon Augmented AI (A2I)
services.desc: Adds human review to machine learning predictions, sending low-confidence results to people to check.

services.name: Amazon Rekognition
services.desc: Image and video analysis: detect objects, text, faces and unsafe content with an API call.

services.name: Amazon Polly
services.desc: Turns text into lifelike speech in dozens of languages and voices.

services.name: Amazon Lex
services.desc: Builds chatbots and voice bots that understand natural language, using the same technology as Alexa.

services.name: Amazon CodeGuru Profiler
services.desc: Profiles running Java and Python apps to find the most expensive lines of code and suggest fixes.

categories.name: Networking and Content Delivery
categories.blurb: Private networks, DNS, and getting content to users quickly.

services.name: Amazon VPC
services.desc: Your own private, isolated network in AWS, with subnets, route tables, gateways and firewalls.

services.name: Amazon CloudFront
services.desc: Global content delivery network that caches your site, APIs and video close to users.

services.name: Amazon Route 53
services.desc: DNS and domain registration, with health checks and traffic routing.

services.name: Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller (ARC)
services.desc: Readiness checks and routing controls for shifting traffic away from an impaired location during recovery.

services.name: Amazon API Gateway
services.desc: Create, publish and secure REST, HTTP and WebSocket APIs in front of Lambda functions or other back ends.

services.name: AWS PrivateLink
services.desc: Private connections from your VPC to AWS services and other VPCs, without traffic crossing the public internet.

services.name: AWS Cloud Map
services.desc: Service discovery: register your app's resources by name so other services can always find them.

services.name: AWS Network Manager
services.desc: A central view for monitoring and managing your global network across AWS and on-premises sites.

services.name: AWS Data Transfer
services.desc: Moving data into, out of and within AWS. It's billed per gigabyte rather than run as a service, and most inbound transfer is free.

categories.name: App Integration
categories.blurb: Connect services together with queues, events, notifications and workflows.

services.name: Amazon SQS
services.desc: Fully managed message queues that let parts of your app hand work to each other reliably.

services.name: Amazon SNS
services.desc: Publish-subscribe messaging that fans messages out to queues, functions, email, SMS and mobile push.

services.name: Amazon EventBridge
services.desc: Serverless event bus that routes events between AWS services, SaaS apps and your own code, plus a scheduler.

services.name: AWS Step Functions
services.desc: Visual workflows that coordinate Lambda functions and AWS services, with retries and error handling built in.

services.name: Amazon Simple Workflow Service (SWF)
services.desc: An older service for coordinating multi-step background jobs and tracking their state.

services.name: Amazon MQ
services.desc: Managed Apache ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ message brokers, for apps that already use those protocols.

services.name: AWS B2B Data Interchange
services.desc: Automates the exchange and transformation of EDI business documents such as orders and invoices with trading partners.

categories.name: Web, Mobile and Messaging
categories.blurb: Build front ends, sign users in, and reach them by email and chat.

services.name: AWS Amplify
services.desc: Build, deploy and host full-stack web and mobile apps, with Git-based CI/CD and managed back ends.

services.name: AWS AppSync
services.desc: Managed GraphQL and real-time APIs that connect apps to data sources like DynamoDB and Lambda.

services.name: Amazon Cognito
services.desc: User sign-up and sign-in for your apps, with social and enterprise logins and secure tokens.

services.name: Amazon Cognito Sync
services.desc: An older Cognito feature that syncs user profile data across a user's devices.

services.name: Amazon Location Service
services.desc: Maps, places search, routing and geofencing APIs for adding location features to apps.

services.name: Amazon Simple Email Service (SES)
services.desc: Send and receive email at scale, for transactional and marketing messages.

services.name: AWS End User Messaging Social
services.desc: Send and receive WhatsApp messages with customers from your AWS applications.

categories.name: Developer Tools
categories.blurb: Write, build, test, deploy and debug code.

services.name: AWS CodeBuild
services.desc: Managed build service that compiles code, runs tests and produces deployable packages.

services.name: AWS CodePipeline
services.desc: Continuous delivery pipelines that automate the build, test and deploy steps of every release.

services.name: AWS CodeDeploy
services.desc: Automates code deployments to EC2, on-premises servers, Lambda and ECS, with rollbacks.

services.name: AWS CodeCommit
services.desc: Private Git repositories hosted on AWS.

services.name: AWS CodeArtifact
services.desc: Private package repository for npm, PyPI, Maven, NuGet and other package formats.

services.name: AWS Cloud9
services.desc: Browser-based IDE for writing, running and debugging code.

services.name: AWS CloudShell
services.desc: A browser-based terminal with the AWS CLI already installed and signed in as you.

services.name: AWS X-Ray
services.desc: Traces requests as they travel through your app, to find slow spots and errors.

services.name: AWS AppConfig
services.desc: Safely roll out feature flags and app configuration changes, with validation and automatic rollback.

services.name: AWS SDKs and Tools
services.desc: Official software development kits, the AWS CLI and IDE toolkits for working with AWS from your own code.

categories.name: Management and Governance
categories.blurb: Provision, monitor, audit and operate everything in your account.

services.name: AWS Management Console
services.desc: The web interface for using every AWS service.

services.name: AWS Console Mobile Application
services.desc: Check resources, alarms and billing from your phone.

services.name: AWS CloudFormation
services.desc: Infrastructure as code: describe your resources in a template and AWS creates, updates and deletes them together.

services.name: AWS Cloud Control API
services.desc: One consistent set of create, read, update, delete and list APIs for hundreds of AWS resource types.

services.name: Amazon CloudWatch
services.desc: Metrics, dashboards and alarms for your AWS resources and applications.

services.name: Amazon CloudWatch Logs
services.desc: Collect, store, search and analyze log files from your apps and AWS services.

services.name: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus
services.desc: Managed, Prometheus-compatible monitoring for container and Kubernetes metrics.

services.name: AWS CloudTrail
services.desc: Records who did what in your account: every API call and console action, for auditing and troubleshooting.

services.name: AWS Config
services.desc: Tracks how your resources are configured over time and checks them against your rules.

services.name: AWS Systems Manager
services.desc: Operate servers at scale: patching, remote sessions, run commands, inventory and parameter storage.

services.name: AWS Systems Manager for SAP
services.desc: Automates operations such as backup and restore for SAP applications running on AWS.

services.name: AWS Health
services.desc: Personalized alerts about AWS events and scheduled maintenance that affect your resources.

services.name: AWS User Notifications
services.desc: A central place to see and route notifications from AWS services.
services.note: Creating your own notification configurations isn't available.

services.name: AWS Compute Optimizer
services.desc: Recommends better-fitting, often cheaper, sizes for EC2, Lambda, EBS and ECS based on actual usage.

services.name: AWS Well-Architected Tool
services.desc: Reviews your workloads against AWS best practices for security, reliability, cost and performance.

services.name: AWS License Manager
services.desc: Tracks and enforces software licenses (Microsoft, Oracle, SAP and others) across AWS and on-premises.

services.name: AWS Resource Explorer
services.desc: Search for any resource in your account by name, tag or type.

services.name: AWS Resource Groups
services.desc: Group resources by tag or stack so you can view and act on them together.

services.name: AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM)
services.desc: Share resources such as subnets and license configurations with other AWS accounts.

services.name: Service Quotas
services.desc: View the limits on each AWS service in your account and request increases.

services.name: AWS Support
services.desc: Help from AWS: documentation, forums, the Health Dashboard and support cases.

services.name: AWS Marketplace
services.desc: A catalog of third-party software, data and AI models you can subscribe to and run on AWS.
services.note: Only free listings and Bedrock model offers are available.

categories.name: Security, Identity and Compliance
categories.blurb: Control who can do what, protect secrets and keys, and block attacks.

services.name: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
services.desc: Users, roles and policies that control exactly who can access which AWS resources.

services.name: AWS Security Token Service (STS)
services.desc: Issues temporary, limited-privilege credentials for users and applications.

services.name: Amazon Verified Permissions
services.desc: Fine-grained authorization for your own apps, written as policies in the Cedar language.

services.name: AWS Directory Service
services.desc: Managed Microsoft Active Directory in AWS, or a connector to your existing directory.

services.name: AWS Key Management Service (KMS)
services.desc: Create and control the encryption keys that protect your data across AWS services.

services.name: AWS Secrets Manager
services.desc: Store, rotate and retrieve database passwords, API keys and other secrets.

services.name: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)
services.desc: Free public SSL/TLS certificates for your AWS-hosted sites, renewed automatically.

services.name: AWS Payment Cryptography
services.desc: Managed cryptographic operations for card payment processing, such as PIN and card-verification handling.

services.name: AWS Signer
services.desc: Code signing, so you can make sure only trusted, unaltered code runs in Lambda and containers.

services.name: AWS WAF
services.desc: Web application firewall that filters malicious traffic such as SQL injection and bots before it reaches your app.

services.name: AWS Artifact
services.desc: On-demand access to AWS compliance reports and agreements, such as SOC and ISO reports.
services.note: HIPAA Business Associate and SEC rule addendums aren't available.

categories.name: Cost Management
categories.blurb: See, budget and control what you spend.

services.name: AWS Billing and Cost Management
services.desc: Your bills, payments, credits and Free Tier usage, all in one console.

services.name: AWS Budgets
services.desc: Set spending or usage budgets and get alerts before you go over them.

services.name: AWS Cost Explorer
services.desc: Charts and reports that break down your costs and usage over time, with forecasts.

categories.name: Internet of Things
categories.blurb: Connect, manage and secure devices, and model the physical world.

services.name: AWS IoT Core
services.desc: Connects devices to the cloud securely and routes their messages to other AWS services.

services.name: AWS IoT Device Management
services.desc: Register, organize, monitor and remotely update fleets of IoT devices.

services.name: AWS IoT Device Defender
services.desc: Audits IoT device security settings and detects unusual device behavior.

services.name: AWS IoT SiteWise
services.desc: Collects and organizes data from industrial equipment so you can monitor and analyze it.

services.name: AWS IoT TwinMaker
services.desc: Builds digital twins: live 3D models of buildings, factories and equipment linked to real data.

categories.name: Migration
categories.blurb: Move existing servers and workloads to AWS.

services.name: AWS Transform MGN
services.desc: Lift-and-shift migration of physical, virtual and cloud servers to AWS, with continuous replication and cutovers measured in minutes. Formerly AWS Application Migration Service.
